full_name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework team (Trustworthy & Responsible AI program)
mission: NIST's Information Technology Laboratory wrote the AI RMF, a voluntary, sector-neutral framework organised around four functions — Govern, Map, Measure, Manage — that organisations use to identify and manage AI risks. The team maintains the Playbook, profiles for specific uses (generative AI, critical infrastructure), and the AI Resource Center.

key_work.title: AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0, NIST AI 100-1)
key_work.plain_summary: A voluntary playbook-style framework that helps any organisation govern, map, measure and manage AI risks; widely used as the US baseline.

key_work.title: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
key_work.plain_summary: Applies the RMF to generative AI, listing 12 risks (e.g. CBRN information, confabulation, information security) and suggested actions.

key_work.title: Concept Note: AI RMF Profile on Trustworthy AI in Critical Infrastructure
key_work.plain_summary: Starts a profile to guide critical-infrastructure operators on managing risks when they adopt AI (April 2026).

key_work.title: Cyber AI Profile (NIST IR 8596, preliminary draft)
key_work.plain_summary: A Cybersecurity Framework profile on securing AI systems, using AI for cyber defence, and thwarting AI-enabled attacks.

key_work.title: NIST AI RMF Playbook
key_work.plain_summary: Suggested actions and documentation practices for achieving each outcome in the framework.

status_note: AI RMF 1.0 published 26 Jan 2023; Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1) July 2024. Since the July 2025 White House AI Action Plan, NIST says 'the AI RMF 1.0 is being revised' (no revised draft published as of Oct 2026). Lead author Elham Tabassi left NIST in early 2025 for Brookings.

Co-author of the Generative AI Profile; former NIST research scientist

warnings.text: AI risks can harm individuals, organisations and society and are often hard to measure.
Generative AI can lower barriers to CBRN information, confabulate, and create new information-security risks.

recommendations.text: Organisations should build a risk-management culture around four functions: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage.
Measure trustworthiness characteristics (valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent, explainable, privacy-enhanced, fair).
Tailor the framework with sector or technology profiles.
